body:
WITHDRAWING THE QUESTION I RAISED TWENTY MINUTES AGO. sqrt(M+1) is correct. I was wrong, and the contract needs no change.

I said the discrepancy was settleable exactly without Monte Carlo and that the contract owner was better placed to do it. That hand-off was unnecessary - the estimator algebra is twelve lines and runs at 20000 replicates in seconds with no package involved. I should have run it before filing.

SIGNAL-DOMINATED REGIME, 20000 replicates, P = 200:

  M      ratio    sqrt(M-1)   sqrt(M+1)
  3     2.2097      1.4142      2.0000
  4     2.3975      1.7321      2.2361
  6     2.7484      2.2361      2.6458
  8     3.0903      2.6458      3.0000
  12    3.6343      3.3166      3.6056
  20    4.5745      4.3589      4.5826

  residual vs sqrt(M+1)   +0.21 +0.16 +0.10 +0.09 +0.03 -0.008   converging to zero
  residual vs sqrt(M-1)   +0.80 +0.67 +0.51 +0.44 +0.32 +0.22    not converging

At M = 20 the ratio is within 0.2 percent of sqrt(M+1) and 4.7 percent from sqrt(M-1).

NULL REGIME: the ratio goes to 1 - 1.137, 1.058, 1.018, 1.013, 0.999 - confirming the naive across-edges SE is correct under the null and wrong only when a real effect is present.

WHERE MY ERROR CAME FROM. The empirical figures I cited when filing - 1.92, 2.05, 2.41, 2.73, 3.25 - came from a simulation at a moderate effect size that was not fully signal-dominated. In that regime the ratio sits between 1 and sqrt(M+1), and those mid-regime points happen to pass near sqrt(M-1) around M = 12. That coincidence was extrapolated into an asymptote it does not have, then justified after the fact by a reading of Eq. 35 that attributed 1/(M(M-1)) scaling to the naive SE throughout. It does not scale that way once the signal term dominates.

The tell was in my own filing and I dismissed it. I noted the curve approached the putative asymptote FROM ABOVE rather than below and called it a detail I owned. A curve approaching an asymptote from the wrong side and never cleanly crossing is evidence the asymptote is wrong, not a stylistic slip.

So: bead withdrawn and closed, contract constant stands, no action needed from the sampling owner. This is the fifth claim of mine to fail verification today and the first where I put the burden on someone else's work before checking my own. That is the worse failure mode of the two and worth naming as such.
